test_title: PYST 59: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the highlighted text in the given sentence.

The minister was** in partnership** with the queen in poisoning the King.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (in cahoots)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"in partnership"** used in the sentence implies collaboration or working together, often with a hint of secrecy or conspiracy. (साझेदारी)

 
 
• **Example:** The two companies were in partnership to create a new product.
 
 
 
• **"In cahoots"** means being in secret agreement or conspiracy, typically for a dishonest purpose. (सांठगांठ में)
 
 
• **Example:** The robbers were in cahoots with the security guard to execute the theft.
 
 
 
• Hence, "in cahoots" is the most appropriate idiom to replace the highlighted text.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (in cahoots)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Run amok** (उन्मत्त हो जाना): To behave uncontrollably or wildly.

 
 
• **Example:** The crowd ran amok after the unexpected announcement.
 
 
 
• **In the blues** (उदास): Feeling sad or depressed.
 
 
• **Example:** After losing the game, he was in the blues for the entire evening.
 
 
 
• **At one's beck and call** (आदेश का पालन करने के लिए तैयार): Always ready to obey someone's orders or wishes.
 
 
• **Example:** The servants were always at the king's beck and call.
